6. Xiang Deng, Yu Gu, Boyuan Zheng, Shijie Chen, Samuel Stevens, Boshi Wang, Huan Sun, and Yu Su. Mind2web: Towards a generalist agent for the web. In Thirty-seventh Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems Datasets and Benchmarks Track, 2023. URL https://openreview.net/forum?id=kiYqbO3wqw.

# abstract
Despite the potential of language model-based agents to solve real-world tasks such as web navigation, current methods still struggle with long-horizon tasks with complex action trajectories. In contrast, humans can flexibly solve complex tasks by learning reusable task workflows from past experiences and using them to guide future actions. To build agents that can similarly benefit from this process, we introduce Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), a method for inducing commonly reused routines, i.e., workflows, and selectively providing workflows to the agent to guide subsequent generations. AWM flexibly applies to both offline and online scenarios, where agents induce workflows from training examples beforehand or from test queries on the fly. We experiment on two major web navigation benchmarks — Mind2Web and WebArena — that collectively cover 1000+ tasks from 200+ domains across travel, shopping, and social media, among others. AWM substantially improves the baseline results by 24.6% and 51.1% relative success rate on Mind2Web and WebArena while reducing the number of steps taken to solve WebArena tasks successfully. Furthermore, online AWM robustly generalizes in cross-task, website, and domain evaluations, surpassing baselines from 8.9 to 14.0 absolute points as train-test task distribution gaps widen.

# Related Work

## Web Navigation Environments and Benchmarks

Early work on web-based agents established foundational environments for studying autonomous navigation. Shi et al. [1] introduced World of Bits, an open-domain platform that framed web interaction as a reinforcement learning problem, enabling agents to operate across a broad range of web tasks. Building on this paradigm, Liu et al. [2] proposed workflow-guided exploration for RL agents acting on web interfaces, demonstrating that structured, reusable action routines can significantly improve exploration efficiency — a key intuition that directly motivates Agent Workflow Memory (AWM). As the field shifted toward large language models, Yao et al. [3] introduced WebShop, a scalable benchmark for grounded language agents performing product-search tasks, highlighting the promise of LLM-driven agents for realistic web interaction. More recently, Zhou et al. [4] released WebArena, a realistic and challenging environment featuring complex, long-horizon tasks across multiple live-style websites, serving as one of the two primary benchmarks on which we evaluate AWM. Koh et al. [5] extended this setting with VisualWebArena, incorporating multimodal observations to stress-test agents on visually grounded web tasks, underscoring the growing complexity of real-world web environments. To support generalist web agents at scale, Deng et al. [6] curated Mind2Web, a large-scale dataset spanning 1,000+ tasks across 100+ real websites covering diverse domains such as travel, shopping, and social media, which constitutes our second evaluation benchmark. Together, these benchmarks reflect an evolution from narrow, simulated environments toward rich, realistic, and diverse web settings — precisely the regime in which AWM's ability to induce and reuse task workflows across long-horizon, cross-domain tasks provides the greatest advantage.

# Related Work

## Web Navigation Environments and Benchmarks

Web-based agent research began with environments like World of Bits [1] and workflow-guided RL exploration [2], where the value of reusable action routines was first demonstrated — directly motivating AWM. The field then shifted toward LLM-driven agents, with WebShop [3] providing an early scalable benchmark for grounded web interaction. More recently, WebArena [4] and VisualWebArena [5] introduced realistic, long-horizon web tasks with multimodal observations, while Mind2Web [6] offered broad coverage across 1,000+ tasks spanning diverse domains. AWM is evaluated on WebArena and Mind2Web, tackling the complex, cross-domain settings these benchmarks define.

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

function.name: write
function.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

function.name: bash
function.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

function.name: find
function.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

function.name: ls
function.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

function.name: workflow_plan
function.description: Register a hierarchical workflow plan. Provide 3-5 main steps at the top level with description, outputFiles, verifiers, and optional children.
